target.title: fix(dock): avoid shell interpolation when adding Dock items
target.body:
## Summary

`DockService.addToDockImpl` built a `bash -c` script that interpolated the caller-supplied path into a single-quoted `defaults write ... -array-add '...'` command. A path containing a single quote (or other shell metacharacters once the quote is closed) can break out of that script and run arbitrary commands as the Peekaboo user, then still restart Dock via `killall`.

This PR:

- validates that the path is absolute and free of control characters;
- XML-escapes the path inside the Dock tile plist fragment;
- invokes `/usr/bin/defaults` and `/usr/bin/killall` directly with argv (no shell);
- adds unit coverage for path validation / XML escaping;
- includes a standalone proof script for the no-shell argv construction.

## Failure scenario

1. An automation or MCP path reaches `addToDock` with a crafted path such as `/tmp/x'; touch /tmp/pwned; echo '`.
2. The path is embedded inside the bash single-quoted tile payload.
3. The unfixed script is executed via `/bin/bash -c`.
4. The shell runs the injected command before/around `defaults write`.

## Verification

- `swiftc -parse-as-library -o /tmp/prove-dock scripts/prove-dock-add-no-shell.swift && /tmp/prove-dock` → `PROOF_OK`
- `swift build` in `Core/PeekabooAutomationKit` → complete
- Full XCTest/Swift Testing not run here (host has Command Line Tools only; no full Xcode.app). CI `macos-ci` is the authoritative suite.

## Scope

Dock add path only. Launch/remove/right-click Dock actions are unchanged.
